source_candidate.display_label: Leanstral 1.5 independently confirms open-weight agentic RL for formal proof engineering

published_claim.summary: Mistral reports Leanstral 1.5 as a 119B-total/approximately-6B-active Apache-2.0 Lean 4 model trained by mid-training, SFT and CISPO RL in multiturn theorem and code-agent environments. Vendor results include 100% miniF2F validation/test, 587/672 PutnamBench, FATE-H 87 and FATE-X 34, with final checking via a SafeVerify fork.

official_artifact_support.status: strong for inference/deployment; incomplete for training reproduction
observations: Official Apache-2.0 model weights are public and the hosted labs-leanstral-1-5 endpoint is documented.

The vendor describes the two RL environments and SafeVerify-based final checking, but this audit did not find a released end-to-end CISPO training corpus/orchestrator sufficient to reproduce the trained model from scratch.
The public inference surface therefore makes proof-generation experiments reproducible without making the training claim itself independently reproducible.

external_evidence.type: public non-vendor result archive; uploader affiliation/independence not established in this audit
observations: Archive states that it preserves generated Lean files, interactive trajectories, per-attempt metadata, compilation/SafeVerify logs and problem summaries for labs-leanstral-1-5.

It reports miniF2F fixed-budget 202/244 pass@1 and 232/244 pass@4, with 233/244 after targeted extended-compute rescue; this does not reproduce the vendor's 100% miniF2F headline under the archive's stated budget/protocol.

It reports ProofNet 39/186 pass@1, 42/186 pass@4, 99/186 pass@8 strict lower bound, and 113/186 only after targeted 16M/32M-token rescue. These results demonstrate substantial working proof capability and strong test-time dependence without serving as a like-for-like reproduction of the vendor benchmark suite.
external_evidence.scope_guard: Do not treat differing miniF2F numbers as a contradiction without a matched evaluation protocol, prompt, tool environment, sampling policy, theorem normalization, token budget and rescue policy.

observations: A fresh self-contained clauseHolds monotonicity lemma was solved and independently checked by Lean with zero sorries and no axioms.

A nominal re-proof of an existing Aeneas leaf was correctly invalidated after transcript inspection showed Leanstral grepped and copied the existing source proof, demonstrating that reference-proof leakage can create false-looking reproduction success unless source and .olean access are isolated.
With genuine isolation, the same Aeneas-style leaf failed at 45 turns without MCP: zero proof attempts and budget exhausted on framework orientation.

A stronger 90-turn run with Lean-LSP MCP engaged deeply but still failed to converge, ending with elaboration errors plus a sorry. This is concrete negative evidence for cold Aeneas-simulation proof authoring under that tested budget/environment, not for Leanstral or agentic proof engineering generally.
external_evidence.scope_guard: The negative result is limited to the tested Aeneas-simulation leaf, isolation procedure, model endpoint, toolchain, budgets and prompt.

external_evidence.type: independent mathlib-style transfer trials derived from the ordeal harness
observations: A core-Lean scheduling-flavored smoke theorem was solved axiom-clean in an out-of-repository sandbox with no path leakage.

An isolated re-derivation of gale's task_utilization_bounded omitted the repository's helper lemmas; Leanstral produced a different valid Mathlib proof path, checked axiom-clean under the trial toolchain.
A genuinely new theorem rmaBound_le_one was also solved axiom-clean with leak scan clean.

The two Mathlib target trials were run under ordeal's Lean 4.30-rc2 + Mathlib rather than gale's pinned Lean 4.27.0, so exact verbatim portability to gale's production toolchain remained an explicit landing caveat in the issue.
external_evidence.scope_guard: This is strong domain-transfer evidence for self-contained Mathlib-style proof synthesis, not a reproduction of Mistral's reported miniF2F/Putnam/FATE numbers or the RL training mechanism.

assessment.result: Worker C87 is materially strengthened but also narrowed. Open weights plus public API make Leanstral 1.5 a genuinely reproducible inference baseline. External oracle-checked trials independently show successful axiom-clean proof synthesis on self-contained/mathlib-style tasks and repo-aware reuse, while clean-room Aeneas-simulation trials failed under tested budgets even with Lean-LSP MCP. This supports the worker's central claim that agentic proof engineering is real, but shows capability is sharply substrate/domain dependent.
what_is_reproduced: Leanstral 1.5 can be invoked as an interactive Lean agent and can produce Lean-accepted proofs on fresh/self-contained obligations.
Live Lean feedback and repository navigation are operationally meaningful parts of the agentic workflow.
Domain transfer is non-uniform: self-contained Mathlib-style tasks can succeed while unfamiliar framework-heavy Aeneas proofs can fail honestly under finite budget.
what_is_not_reproduced: Mistral's exact 100% miniF2F, 587/672 PutnamBench, FATE-H 87, FATE-X 34 or five-new-bugs headline numbers under a matched protocol.
The causal claim that CISPO RL specifically produced the observed agentic behavior versus other training stages; no matched ablation was found here.
End-to-end recreation of the training run from released data/code.
A compact typed controller separated from the full autoregressive model, explicit action propensities, or cost-aware/OPE controller evaluation.

reproducibility_risks: Reference proof leakage through readable source or .olean can invalidate apparent re-derivation success; clean-room source isolation plus transcript path scan is required.
Lean/Mathlib version drift can change lemma names and must be checked by the target repository's own oracle.
Vendor and external benchmark numbers are not comparable without matched token budgets, prompts, tool environments, rescue policy and theorem preprocessing.
Hosted Labs model behavior may change or retire independently of the released weight snapshot; record exact model id, date, harness and tool versions.

recommended_downstream_use.evidence_effect: Upgrade C87's artifact/reproducibility support for the existence and practical utility of full-model agentic Lean proof engineering; retain vendor headline benchmark numbers as primary-study results unless matched independently.
recommended_downstream_use.experiment_design: Use Leanstral as a full-model capability baseline with Lean as sole oracle. Require source/olean isolation for re-derivation tests, transcript leak scanning, target-toolchain compilation, #print axioms checks, explicit token/turn/time budgets and domain-stratified results. Do not infer compact-controller performance from full-model success.

exact_next_action: Search for an independent, protocol-matched reproduction of Leanstral's miniF2F/Putnam/FATE results or a released immutable benchmark manifest that explains the gap between vendor 100% miniF2F and the public 95.5%-after-rescue archive. If unavailable, rotate to another under-audited C11 namespace with executable artifacts and a plausible independent reproduction/failure trail.
